candidate_relations.reason: Idiopathic orbital inflammation is a diagnosis of exclusion; histology shows central necrobiosis with abundant Alcian-blue mucin, the GA pattern, not nonspecific IOI.
Extensive mucin makes a myxoid granuloma description, but the required diagnosis is granuloma annulare with necrobiosis.
Periocular granuloma annulare is the same entity as granuloma annulare at this inferior orbital-rim nodule with necrobiosis and mucin.
A chalazion is a meibomian lipogranuloma of the tarsus, not a rim nodule after DCR whose biopsy shows necrobiosis and pools of mucin.
Granuloma faciale is a facial vasculitis with Grenz zone, not palisading necrobiosis with Alcian-blue mucin.
Ziehl–Neelsen and Grocott stains are negative and there is no necrosis of infection type, so mycobacterial infection is not the necrobiotic-mucin lesion.
